question: In the Union Budget 2025-26, a Maritime Development Fund of Rs. _________ crore over 10 years has been announced.
solution:
The correct answer is __**25000 crore**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Maritime Development Fund** was announced in the **Union Budget 2025-26** with a fund allocation of **Rs. 25,000 crore** to be utilized over a period of 10 years. 
• The purpose of this fund is to enhance the development of the maritime sector, which includes **ports, shipping, and waterways infrastructure** in India. 
• This fund aims to support initiatives such as **modernization of ports**, expansion of shipping facilities, and development of inland waterways to improve logistics efficiency. 
• The maritime sector is critical for India's economy as it handles about **95% of the country's trade by volume** and contributes significantly to reducing transportation costs. 
• The creation of the Maritime Development Fund aligns with the government's vision of transforming India into a global maritime hub under the **Sagarmala Programme**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Importance of the Maritime Sector:** 
• India has a coastline of about **7,517 kilometers**, making the maritime sector essential for trade and logistics. 
• The sector supports **employment generation**, boosts exports, and strengthens international trade partnerships. 
• Ports like **Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata** are key contributors to India's export-import activities. 
• **Sagarmala Programme:** 
• This flagship initiative was launched by the Government of India to enhance port-led development. 
• It focuses on port modernization, connectivity improvement, **port-linked industrialization**, and coastal community development. 
• The Sagarmala Programme aims to reduce logistics costs for both domestic and EXIM (Export-Import) cargo. 
• **Inland Waterways Development:** 
• India has about **14,500 kilometers** of navigable inland waterways. 
• The government has been promoting the use of waterways for cargo transportation through projects like **National Waterway-1 (NW-1)** on the Ganga River. 
• This mode of transport is environmentally friendly and cost-effective compared to road and rail transportation. 
• **Global Maritime Trends:** 
• Many countries are investing in **green shipping**, automation, and digitalization of ports to enhance efficiency and sustainability. 
• India's Maritime Development Fund aligns with these global trends by promoting **modern infrastructure** and eco-friendly practices. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Maritime India Vision 2030:** 
• This document outlines the strategic roadmap for India's maritime sector till 2030. 
• It includes plans for port capacity expansion, digital transformation, and integration of sustainable practices. 
• The Maritime Development Fund will play a crucial role in achieving the goals set under this vision. 
• **Economic Impact:** 
• Investments in the maritime sector can significantly contribute to India's **GDP growth**. 
• Efficient ports and waterways reduce logistics costs, making Indian exports more competitive globally. 
• This fund supports the government's aim to achieve a **$5 trillion economy**. </ul
